structure.purpose: Project manifest (project-manifest@1): name (= hub folder /projects/<name>), repo, relation to AXF, shared data. Nothing is loaded or compiled without a valid one.
App identity, framework version, targets and the default asset for every slot.
Framework version + template the app was initialized from, with a hash of every baked file.
The baked framework runtime (core engines, React components, CSS, schemas).

Baked framework libraries: `settings` (the settings interface every app ships: Appearance, Account & security, Connections, Plugins, About) and `alerts`. Plugins add groups or sub-tabs to Settings → Plugins; they never ship a settings screen of their own.
Hot-swappable assets, one folder per asset type; read at build time by app/axf-assets.ts.
The app's views; nav assets reference them by id.
Binds this app's handlers to the standard action vocabulary.
Next.js root layout: loads the manifest + assets on the server and hands them to the client-side AXF runtime.
The single route that mounts the AXF shell (the shell routes views itself).
Client component: creates the runtime once, registers actions, renders AppShell after mount (no SSR of browser state).
